methodological_rigor.justification: This is a single-center retrospective cohort comparing 38 NTRK-fusion PTCs vs 1196 BRAFV600E PTCs with clearly defined inclusion/exclusion criteria, standardized FNAB+NGS workflow, dual-radiologist ultrasound consensus and re-review of pathology per 2022 WHO classification. However, the NTRK cohort is small (38 patients), follow-up is short (median 16 months), and there is no multivariable adjustment for confounders when comparing groups with highly imbalanced sample sizes. Statistical methods (t/Mann-Whitney, chi-square/Fisher, univariate logistic regression, ROC) are appropriate but no multiplicity correction is performed despite many pairwise comparisons, and no sample-size or power calculation is reported; effect sizes are mostly presented as ORs with 95% CIs only for the primary LLNM analysis.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The study is a retrospective single-center cohort of consecutive PTC cases with molecular testing, best classified as Oxford LoE 4 given its low-quality cohort design with limited follow-up and no external validation. Findings have plausible translational value—suggesting preoperative molecular/ultrasound features (size >12 mm, wider-than-tall shape, isoechogenicity) could identify NTRK-fusion PTC for tailored surgical planning and TRK-inhibitor candidacy—but the work does not demonstrate that incorporating these markers changes outcomes. Impact is incremental rather than practice-changing.

reporting_quality.justification: As an observational comparative cohort study, STROBE is the applicable standard. Most key STROBE items are covered: study design, setting, participants with inclusion/exclusion, variables, data sources (ultrasound machines and sequencing panel specified), statistical methods, and limitations. Missing or underdeveloped items include a flow diagram of participant selection, explicit reporting of missing data handling, and confounder adjustment strategy. No data-availability statement is provided and no code/data repository is referenced; raw data sharing is not mentioned, so data availability scores 1.

novelty_literature.justification: The paper extends prior NTRK-fusion PTC characterization by using an unselected consecutively accrued cohort and by directly contrasting NTRK-fusion vs BRAFV600E clinicopathology and sonography, which the authors argue has not been systematically reported. Findings such as NTRK1 association with bilateral involvement, the 12 mm ultrasound cutoff for LLNM risk, and a hobnail-variant RBPMS-NTRK3 case add incremental detail. However, the core observations (follicular patterns, high LNM, younger age, high TBSRTC category spread) largely confirm multiple prior series cited throughout, so novelty is moderate rather than paradigm-shifting.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well organized into clear subsections, with a structured abstract, logically sequenced results mirroring the stated aims, and a discussion that methodically contextualizes each finding against prior literature. Tables and a figure are described with sufficient detail for interpretation, and statistical results are consistently paired with effect estimates and P values. Minor issues include dense comparative paragraphs that could be tightened, occasional awkward phrasing, and some reliance on narrative citation rather than quantitative synthesis.

key_strengths: Unselected consecutive preoperative-molecularly-tested PTC cohort enabling direct NTRK-fusion vs BRAFV600E comparison
Standardized workflow: central FNAB with NGS 13-gene/7-fusion panel, dual-radiologist ultrasound review, and pathology re-review under 2022 WHO criteria
Clinically actionable preoperative risk marker identified (tumor diameter >12 mm on ultrasound: OR 5.00, 95% CI 1.10-22.82) with ROC cutoff analysis
Novel description of NTRK1 association with bilateral lobe involvement and a hobnail-variant RBPMS-NTRK3 case
key_concerns: Small NTRK-fusion sample (n=38) limits power and precludes multivariable adjustment; comparator arm (n=1196) is highly imbalanced
No multiplicity correction across numerous pairwise comparisons and no a priori power calculation
Short median follow-up (16 months) precludes meaningful recurrence or survival inferences
Single-center Chinese cohort with no external validation; generalizability to other populations uncertain
No data-availability statement and no code or dataset sharing
chief_reviewer.rationale: Competent, well-reported single-center retrospective cohort with appropriate but not advanced statistics; findings are incremental and translationally plausible but not practice-changing, fitting a mid-impact oncology journal (Tier 3) with minor revisions addressing multiplicity and data sharing.
